findings.claim: metal sintering produces a slightly rough surface (powder granules) but close to the finish of machined metal.
findings.truth: Metal laser powder-bed fusion can leave layer artefacts and adhered particles. A smooth or specified finish may need machining or polishing.
findings.evidence: NIST, Contour parameters, melt pool behavior, and surface roughness relationships across laser powder bed fusion platforms and metallic alloys (2025); NIST AMB2018-01 benchmark

findings.claim: MIG welding is shielded by an inert gas (argon or CO₂).
findings.truth: MIG uses an inert shielding gas such as argon. Carbon dioxide is used in the broader GMAW process, including active-gas mixtures for mild steel, but it is not inert.
findings.evidence: American Welding Society, What Is GMAW? (2025), lines 454–459 and 481–486

findings.claim: MIG welding shields the molten pool from oxygen using a flow of _____ gas such as argon or CO2.
findings.truth: Argon is inert; carbon dioxide is not. The question must not give carbon dioxide as an example of the inert shielding gas used in MIG.
findings.evidence: American Welding Society, What Is GMAW? (2025), lines 454–459 and 481–486

findings.claim: water quenches fastest ... brine (salt water) quenches fastest of all.
findings.truth: Among the three media named, brine quenches fastest, water is faster than oil, and oil is less severe than water or brine.
findings.evidence: ASM International, One minute mentor: Quenching and Tempering (2021), lines 250–251; ScienceDirect, Quenching Medium overview

findings.claim: A high-speed steel twist drill should be oil quenched and tempered at 150–250 °C.
findings.truth: High-speed-steel heat-treatment schedules depend on the grade and commonly use much higher austenitising and tempering temperatures, often with repeated tempers. A 150–250 °C straw temper is not a general high-speed-steel schedule.
findings.evidence: BÖHLER S730 High Speed Steel data sheet; Uddeholm Heat Treatment guide (high-speed steel: 3 × 560 °C)

findings.claim: Tempering and case hardening are taught as required processes, with supporting questions and flashcards.
findings.truth: Specification 3.2.6 lists normalising, annealing, hardening and quenching only. Options: retain tempering and case hardening explicitly as non-exam enrichment, or remove their sections, practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards from this unit.

findings.claim: Powder coating, polishing and anodising are taught as core surface-finishing processes, with supporting questions and flashcards.
findings.truth: Specification 3.2.7 lists painting, dip coating, electroplating and galvanising only. Options: retain the additional processes explicitly as non-exam enrichment, or remove their sections, practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards from this unit.
Anodising is most commonly used on aluminium, but magnesium and titanium can also be anodised.
findings.evidence: The Welding Institute, What is anodising?; Aluminum Anodizers Council, What is Anodizing?

findings.claim: Anodising is used on aluminium only.
findings.truth: Anodising is most commonly used on aluminium, but it can also be used on magnesium and titanium.
findings.evidence: The Welding Institute, What is anodising?; Aluminum Anodizers Council, What is Anodizing?
